_about: What the narrator says when you step inside, before the away note and the drink offer.
visit: first (only your very first visit), return (coming back) or regular (coming back, once you've spent regular_after_hours in the café; mixed in with the return lines).
when (late night, dawn, morning, afternoon, evening, night) and weather (clear, cloudy, drizzle, rain, heavy_rain, fog, snow) are optional: leave them out for any.
Lines with conditions are picked more often when they fit. There must always be at least one first line and one return line with no conditions.
text can be one line in quotes or a list in [ ] (one is picked). Keep each to about 3 lines of 46 letters.

lines.text: You take the free table by the window. Coffee and Toe Beans is a charming place. If you're lucky, a cat will come by.
The café is small: a few tables, a lot of books, and cats who come and go as they please.
You take the table by the window. Someone has left the lamps on and the menu written on the chalkboard.
You're the first one in this morning. The table by the window is free.
It's late, but the café is still open. The table by the window is free.
You're back. The table by the window is free, as usual.
Your table by the window is waiting.
You sit down at your table by the window.
Back at the table by the window. It feels like yours by now.
The cats barely look up when you come in. You're a regular now.
It's barely light out. The café is quiet, and the lamps are still on.
Good morning. The café smells of coffee.
Morning light on the marble. Your table is free.
The afternoon is slow in the café. Your table is free.
A quiet afternoon. Someone has left a newspaper on the next table.
The lamps are on. A good time to sit for a while.
Evening. The windows across the street are lighting up.
It's late, and the café is quiet. Just the lamps and the cats.
Paris is asleep. The café isn't, quite.
It's very late. The café is still open, just about.
You come in out of the rain. Your table by the window is dry and warm.
Your umbrella drips by the door. The table by the window is free.
You made it in just before the worst of the rain.
A fine drizzle outside. Inside, it's warm.
The fog has hidden half of Paris. The café is right where you left it.
You shake the snow off your coat. The café is warm.
Snow, and the lamps already on. A good evening to be inside.
A clear day. The sun reaches all the way to your table.
A clear night. You can see the Eiffel Tower from your table.
Grey skies over Paris. The lamps make up for it.
The rooftops are wet and shiny. The café is warm and dry.
